$comment: Verdict-to-label map for the L2 review publication step (ADR-087 §B.7). It sits beside labels.yml because it is the same kind of thing: taxonomy data a script applies, not a rule a workflow restates. Every key below is a value of `decision` at the root of a verdict or of `tag` on one of its findings, as .agents/schemas/verdict.schema.json bounds them, and every label is defined in labels.yml — all of them are files in this repository, so .github/workflows/guardrails.yml asserts it. A label this file names is applied when a verdict asks for it. Whether it comes back off when a verdict stops asking is `retire-when-absent` below, and it is a decision per label rather than a rule over all of them: a debt is retired, a fact about the change is not. A label this file does not name is never added and never removed: a repository's own `area:` labels, and anything a human put on the pull request, survive a publication run untouched.

tag.$comment: Keyed off a FINDING's tag, not a verdict-wide one: the publication step reads every finding, so a review reporting a `[CROSS-REPO]` and a `[DOC DEBT]` applies both labels from one verdict. `PHASE` -> `phase-gated` is the fifth mapping and is deferred with its tag: the label exists in labels.yml, the tag is outside the schema's enum until `pr-review.md` is in git, and a mapping off a value a verdict cannot carry is a label nothing ever applies.

retire-when-absent.$comment: Labels the publication takes back off when the current verdict no longer asks for them. A debt belongs here: a `[DOC DEBT]` finding applies `doc-debt`, and a later review that finds nothing has retired it — leaving the label makes the pull request assert a debt its own current review denies, which is what happened on exeris-docs#123. A label that states what the change IS does not belong here, and `cross-repo` is the case: a review raising no cross-repo finding has not made the change single-repo, so the label stands until a human says otherwise. Adding a tag above is therefore two decisions, not one.

remove-on.$comment: A verdict short of BLOCKED takes the block off. `PASS` and `CONDITIONAL` both say the same thing about `hard-block`: this run found nothing that refuses the merge outright. Leaving it on a CONDITIONAL left the label saying the worst answer the review ever gave, which is what the comment above says it must not do. `hard-block` is also listed in `retire-when-absent`, so this block is not load-bearing for it today; it stays because it can name a label the maps above do not, and because deleting it would delete the statement that a PASS is what lifts a block.
